title: The MS Unidirectional Current as a Generalization of the ABC Absorption Current
abstract: For a free scalar particle in one spatial dimension, in a single-pass half-line geometry, we compare the absorbing Robin boundary condition with the generalized Marchewka--Schuss (MS) unidirectional-current family. Robin absorption is characterized by a single parameter $κ>0$: once $κ$ is specified, its momentum-dependent absorption profile is fixed. In the generalized MS construction, by contrast, the detector response is described by a spectral function $λ(k)$, subject to the positivity and subnormalization conditions of the detection law. We show that every Robin choice of $κ$ corresponds to the particular MS calibration $λ_κ(k)=πκ/(k+κ)^2$, which reproduces the complete Robin absorption current for every admissible one-sided spectral amplitude and at every time. Thus the entire one-parameter Robin absorption family is contained within the generalized MS family. The MS construction is more general: the choice $λ_{\rm full}(k)=π/(4k)$ gives unit absorption efficiency for every wave number, which cannot be achieved by any fixed Robin parameter. In this precise sense, the generalized MS detector process extends the Robin absorbing-boundary family. We also compare their asymptotic behavior in the ballistic fixed-ray regime and in the fixed-distance late-time limit.
summary: This paper compares the standard Robin boundary condition model for particle absorption with the more general Marchewka–Schuss (MS) unidirectional current formalism. It proves that the Robin model is a special case of the MS construction, demonstrating that the MS framework is more general by allowing for unit absorption efficiency. This has implications for accurately modeling quantum detection processes in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper compares two theoretical frameworks—the generalized Marchewka–Schuss (MS) unidirectional current and the absorbing Robin boundary condition—used to model particle detection in quantum mechanics.
main_result: The entire one-parameter Robin absorption family is shown to be contained within the more general MS framework, which allows for unit absorption efficiency unattainable by fixed Robin parameters.
method: The comparison involves matching the spectral amplitudes of the absorption currents derived from both the Robin boundary condition and the generalized MS spectral function.
model_or_system: The model considers a free scalar particle propagating in one spatial dimension within a single-pass half-line geometry, analyzed using quantum wave mechanics.
key_observables: Absorption current ($j_{ABC}$ vs $J_{UD}$), absorption probability, and the spectral response function $\lambda(k)$.
important_parameters: The Robin parameter $\kappa > 0$, the spectral response function $\lambda(k)$, and asymptotic regimes (ballistic fixed-ray vs. fixed-distance late-time).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on matching detector statistics and utilizes the stationary phase approximation for asymptotic behavior.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the two models, derives the relationship between their respective spectral functions, proves the containment of the Robin family within the MS family, and compares their asymptotic behavior in different physical limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical generalization of boundary absorption models, which is crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems where particle loss or detection is involved.
